subject: Net terms & invoice ramp — Veridian Health pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Tan <samantha.tan@veridianhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Blythe <marcus.blythe@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Net terms request for pilot / PO & tax docs

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the team is excited to move the pilot forward. A quick question on billing: because Veridian runs centralized vendor payments on a monthly cycle, can Redwood accommodate Net60 on invoices for the initial 3-month pilot? We expect spend of ~$120k across the pilot, with the potential to scale quickly thereafter.

If Net60 is a hard no, would you consider a compromise: 30 days for the first month (to settle initial onboarding costs) and Net60 after that? We can issue a PO once terms are agreed.

Also attached our W-9 and a standardized PO template if it helps: PO_78921_Veridian.pdf and W-9_Veridian.pdf.

Best,
Samantha Tan
Director, Strategic Procurement
Veridian Health

Attachments: W-9_Veridian.pdf (pdf) — PO_78921_Veridian.pdf (pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Tan <samantha.tan@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Net terms request for pilot / PO & tax docs

Hi Samantha — great to hear (and thanks for sending the PO + W-9).

We typically operate on Net30 for new customer pilots to keep cashflow predictable, but we do have a few structured options for customers who need extended windows while we ramp usage:

- Option A (standard): Net30, monthly invoicing in arrears.
- Option B (bridge): 20% upfront deposit at kickoff, then monthly invoices Net45 for months 2–3.
- Option C (extended): Net60 with a credit cap and final settlement on completion (requires a credit check + finance approval).

Given your expected spend (~$120k) and rapid scale potential, we can make Option C available with the following conditions:
1) Signed SOW (received — thanks).
2) PO issued referencing deal HV-2026-0043.
3) A soft credit review (no hard pull) and a maximum credit line of $150k to start.
4) A 30-day credit ramp: first invoice due Net30 for month 1, then Net60 thereafter — or, if you prefer, a 20% deposit to keep Net60 from day one.

I'll loop in Finance (David) to run the soft check and confirm the credit ceiling. If that works, we can send a DocuSign amendment for signatures.

Quick ask: can you confirm the billing entity (Veridian Health, Inc. vs. Veridian Health Labs)? Also, is your payment currency USD?

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Signed_SOW_Veridian_20260108.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Blythe <marcus.blythe@veridianhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Net terms request for pilot / PO & tax docs

Vivek — thanks for the flexible options. A couple clarifications from Veridian:

1) Billing entity is "Veridian Health, Inc." (same as on the W-9).
2) Currency: USD.
3) Given internal approvals, we can do the 20% deposit right away if that shortens procurement lead time, but our finance leadership prefers the low-touch Net60 approach if Redwood will accept a credit cap of $150k.

Can David confirm if a soft credit check and the cap are sufficient, or will you need a parent guarantee / ACH mandate?

Appreciate the help — looking to finalize by next week so we can kick off onboarding the week of Jan 26.

—Marcus
Procurement Manager
Veridian Health

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Net terms request for pilot / PO & tax docs

Internal note — forwarding for approval. Summary: Veridian requests Net60, estimated pilot spend $120k, wants credit cap $150k. They can do 20% deposit if needed; W-9 + signed SOW attached.

Conditions we should consider before approving Net60 with $150k cap:
- Run a soft credit check (no bureau hard pull).
- Require an ACH mandate + primary payment method on file.
- For first invoice: either Net30 or 20% deposit cleared, per Vivek's options.
- Include a clause: any invoice > 60 days past due triggers suspension and reduces credit cap to zero until remitted.

Marissa — do you want to approve this? If not, we should propose the bridge (20% deposit + Net45).

Thanks,
David
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Net terms request for pilot / PO & tax docs

David / Vivek — approving the Net60 request with a $150k credit cap on an interim basis for the pilot only, subject to the following binding conditions:

1) Veridian signs an amendment to the SOW documenting Net60 terms + credit cap (we will send via DocuSign).
2) Veridian provides an ACH mandate OR a valid corporate card to be kept on file (we prefer ACH).
3) We commence a soft credit check; if results indicate any material risk, we reserve the right to revert to bridge terms (20% deposit + Net45).
4) Redwood reserve clause: any single invoice > 60 days unpaid may trigger immediate suspension of service.
5) For tax compliance: US customers must provide W-9; for any EU invoicing we will require VAT registration evidence and specify whether reverse charge applies.

Vivek — please prepare the amendment and outline the billing cadence (initial invoice cadence and subsequent monthly invoices). David — please proceed with the soft credit review and loop in Legal for the amendment language.

Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Tan <samantha.tan@veridianhealth.com>, Marcus Blythe <marcus.blythe@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Net terms request for pilot / PO & tax docs

Hi Samantha / Marcus — good news: we've approved a temporary Net60 arrangement with a $150k credit cap for the pilot, pending the items Marissa outlined. Practical next steps:

1) I'll send a short DocuSign amendment (same day) that: 1) documents Net60 terms for months 2–3, 2) sets the $150k credit cap, and 3) includes the suspension clause.
2) Veridian to either: (a) complete and return the ACH mandate form we attach, or (b) confirm the corporate card to hold on file.
3) David will run a soft credit check today and reply with results; this does not require any action from your AR team.
4) Once the amendment is signed and ACH/card is on file (or 20% deposit is cleared), we will issue the kickoff invoice. Our preference is to invoice in USD monthly in arrears; first invoice will either be Net30 (if no deposit) or reflect the deposit arrangement if Veridian chooses Option B.

Please confirm which path you prefer (Net60 with ACH on file, or 20% deposit + Net45). We'll stand by to route the DocuSign.

Thanks and excited to get started the week of Jan 26.

—Vivek
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments included earlier: Signed_SOW_Veridian_20260108.pdf; referenced forms to be attached to DocuSign amendment."
